subject: NBA game-feed phase verification, failure semantics and access scope

body.content: Hello Sportradar team, Please route this to the NBA API team and, where necessary, the access/licensing team. I'm investigating a phase-evidence source for The Corner, a sports-odds analytical project. This is an inquiry only, not a purchase or subscription authorization. Appropriate access and permitted use have not yet been established for this project. We are evaluating your NBA game-level feed as evidence for a conservative pregame eligibility check. We are not treating scheduled start time, cache duration or fresh HTTP receipt as proof that a game has not started. Please identify the applicable product/API version, endpoint and access tier for your answers. 1. What do scheduled and created guarantee about actual play? Can either remain visible after jump ball during collection failure, publication delay or failover? Does a repeated unchanged status mean the source positively reverified phase? 2. Which field or transport signal identifies the last positive verification of **game status**, rather than a roster/statistics update, cache refresh or HTTP response? Please provide timestamp units, timezone, clock assumptions and scope. 3. How can a client detect lost/partial coverage, data-collection outage, stale cache, replayed responses and failover? Can HTTP 200 and fresh Date coexist with stale phase? Which signals revoke confidence in a prior pregame status? 4. Is any maximum delay from actual jump ball to game-status publication bounded operationally or contractually? Separate collection, publication, caching and delivery. Please identify exceptions and whether these are guarantees or targets. 5. Is game REST status authoritative over schedule status? What should consumers do with conflicts or apparent status regressions? Does any push channel provide status-verification liveness, distinct from event/transport heartbeats? 6. For the v8 play-by-play candidate, what is cache behavior during created, delayed starts, interruption and outages? Do conditional GET/304 responses establish anything about source phase freshness? What call rates are permitted? 7. How should clients distinguish pre-start delay from an interruption after play? How should postponed/replacement games be mapped when IDs are not linked? Are there stable league references and documented correction/reuse semantics? 8. Which NBA season types and coverage levels satisfy your answers? Are preseason, international venues, extended-boxscore coverage or trial data exceptions? 9. Which package/tier permits access to the exact feed and retention of payloads, metadata and derived phase judgments for internal audit/replay? Please confirm applicable trial equivalence, exceptions, retention restrictions and allowed use. 10. Please identify the author/team, effective date, controlling documentation or agreement revision, and how changes/withdrawal of these assurances are notified. An answer that no positive-verification timestamp or maximum latency guarantee exists is useful. We will retain that limitation, not infer a guarantee from tests. Please advise which access route and entitlement documentation are appropriate for this use case. We have not conducted real transition captures under an approved entitlement. Please do not send API keys by email. Thank you, Edward Cooper
